k-1.summary: Two of the three problems are trivial one-step fills (a rhombus is two triangles; a trapezoid is three). The only real task is finding two fillings of the pennant, plus an open-ended 'shop' game. A quick child is done in about 10 minutes, which is exactly the 'dumbed down, ends too early' K–1 failure the organizer has complained about. The outlines are correct and at actual size, but the pages also carry titles, Name/Date fields, a story frame, filler 'tell or show' questions and adult notes that must all go.

grades-2-3.summary: The band never touches its assigned kernel (possible/impossible blue-rhombus boards, up/down counting, fewest-gap packings). It uses a no-shared-colors filling puzzle instead. Only P1 needs any thought (one pennant is forced to be 2 blues + 1 red); P2 and P3 are solved at once with two yellows, or with four reds against six blues. The boards are correct and actual size, but every page repeats the rules and carries a title, Name/Date fields, filler questions, enrichment labels and 'Build first', and a quick child runs out after about 15 minutes.

edits.quote: Kernel 2 is absent: no rhombus tilings of a hexagon. The band reuses the grades 2–3 boards and color rule with a counting twist, so a quick child runs out after about 15 minutes (about 25 minutes missing).
edits.fix: Add a central problem on an actual-size triangular grid: 'Find all the ways to tile this hexagon with blue rhombi.' Start with the 2-2-1 hexagon (6 tilings), then the side-2 hexagon (20 tilings). Give one working board plus small recording copies.

edits.quote: No flips or ribbons, and no work for the last ~15 minutes.
edits.fix: Add a flip problem: define a flip (three rhombi forming a small hexagon, rotated into the other filling). Ask for the fewest flips between two given tilings of the side-2 hexagon, and whether a tiling can return to itself in an odd number of flips. Put the ribbon/left-right path idea in the adult notes as a proof route.

grades-4-5.summary: The three problems are a fewest-pieces version of the grades 2–3 color puzzle on the same two boards. P1 (answer 5) and P3 (answer 10) ask for a real lower-bound argument, but P2 is immediate and the 'Think about' hints hand over the proofs. The band's assigned kernel (hexagon rhombus tilings, flips, ribbons) is missing entirely, and a quick child is done in about 15 minutes. The pages carry the same titles, Name/Date fields, repeated rule boxes and 'Build first' lines as the other bands.

overall.strongest: All outlines are drawn correctly at actual size (1-inch block edges), and the grades 4–5 pennant and no-yellow problems ask for a genuine optimality argument with correct answers of 5 and 10.
overall.weakest: The packet ignores both kernels in the outline: there are no blue-rhombus obstructions or fewest-gap packings for grades 2–3 and no hexagon tilings, flips or ribbons for grades 4–5. K–1 is reduced to trivial one-step fills, and every band runs out of substantial work after 10–15 minutes.
